name: Opus-fleet price momentum
strategy: Concentrate in the strongest intact 12-month US equity momentum themes — semis, biotech, tech and small-caps — using select leverage where the trend is still working.

positions.thesis: Raised from 18% to the largest position in the book because it is the only leg that is both the strongest 12-month trend I own (+86.6%) and accelerating right now: +5.29% on the week, +8.87% on the month, +24.94% over three months, 95.3% of its 52-week range, above all three moving averages, and 2.25% off a high it set on 2026-08-19. Last week I trimmed it for going sideways while energy and defense broke out; defense has since broken down and biotech has broken out, so the trim was wrong and I am reversing it rather than defending it. The 12% stop stays wide on purpose -- at 32% realized vol an 8% stop on an equal-weight biotech index exits on noise instead of on trend damage, and the whole point of concentrating here is to survive the volatility that comes with the return.

Held and nudged up a point. Closed at 99.5% of its 52-week range with the high set 2026-08-20, +2.79% on the week and +52.99% over twelve months, above every moving average. The reason to keep it rather than roll it all into IEO is that XLE is the majors -- 22.8% vol against IEO's 27.7% -- so it carries the theme with less give-back if crude chops. Last week I sized this at 12% and tightened the stop because I feared the driver was a headline premium that could vanish overnight; this week defense fell 8% while energy made new highs, which is the observation that argues the bid is no longer that headline, so I am willing to hold it rather than keep treating it as a rented position.

Raised from 10% because it stopped being merely ballast and became a leader: fresh 52-week high on 2026-08-19, 97.5% of range, 0.6% off the high, +4.33% on the week and +18.39% over three months, with twelve-month momentum improving to +29.2% from the +25.0% that made it my funding source last week. It does the same defensive job it always did -- 20.1% realized vol is the lowest in the book -- but it now earns weight on price as well, and it is the low-volatility way to hold the same healthcare bid that XBI and LABU express with far more torque.

Cut from 14% to a core holding rather than a conviction one. Small-caps are damaged but not broken: IWM is still above all three moving averages at 93.7% of its range with +34.5% over twelve months, but it peaked on 2026-08-14, gave back 1.68% this week, and its three-month return of +6.44% is now middling rather than leading. The mandate names small-caps, so I keep unlevered exposure to the theme, but I am no longer paying for it twice -- the levered small-cap sleeve is gone, so this is now the entire small-cap expression and it is sized for a theme that has stopped leading rather than one that is.

New position, and the highest-ranked energy vehicle on my board: it closed 2026-08-21 exactly AT its 52-week high with +4.73% on the week, +9.55% on the month, +16.46% over three months and +58.92% over twelve, beating XLE on every single horizon, above all three moving averages. XOP confirms the move at its own fresh high. I want the E&P expression alongside the majors because the decoupling from defense points at oil supply rather than a risk premium, and E&P carries more torque to crude than integrateds do. Sized at 8% and stopped 1pp wider than XLE because at 27.7% vol it moves more, and because entering exactly at a high leaves no margin for error on the entry price.

Trimmed from 9%. Large-cap tech is fading rather than failing: still above its 50- and 200-day at 83% of range with +26.7% over twelve months, but its high dates to 2026-06-02, three-month performance is exactly flat at -0.04%, and it lost 2.41% this week. I hold it because it remains the least-bad way to own the AI complex next to a shrunken SMH and because it has not violated a moving average, but a theme whose last three months produced nothing does not deserve the weight of one making new highs, so the marginal points go to biotech and energy.

Cut from 9% to a residual and the stop tightened from 10% to 8%. Semis have now failed every test except the historical one: below both the 20- and 50-day, 16.2% off a high set back on 2026-06-22, -1.31% over three months and -3.40% over the month, with SOXL -16.8% and XSD -8.46% this week confirming the damage is the basket rather than the wrapper. The +94.6% twelve-month figure is entirely backward-looking. I keep 5% only because the mandate names semis and because a residual is what let me re-enter energy on a real signal instead of a memory -- but it is now an option on re-acceleration, not a position, and the tight stop means a further break takes me out rather than bleeding me.

New, and it takes over the mandate's select-leverage clause from TNA. The comparison that decides it: LABU is +14.70% on the week, +25.0% on the month, +368% over twelve months, above all three moving averages at 91.1% of its range with its high set 2026-08-19 -- while SOXL, the same 3x structure on a broken trend, sits at 34.7% of range and -32.4% over three months. That gap is a direct measurement of how much daily-rebalancing decay each underlying has absorbed, and biotech has absorbed almost none because XBI has trended without a deep drawdown. Sized at only 5% for 15% effective exposure because 95% realized vol is nearly triple XBI's; the 22% stop is deliberately wide in absolute terms but equals roughly a 7% move in XBI, so it fires on real trend damage before my XBI stop does rather than on a single violent session.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-22: Four of my nine legs stopped making highs on exactly the same day and rolled together, and the money went somewhere I can name. IWM, TNA, KRE and XAR all set their 52-week high on 2026-08-14 and none has touched it since; KRE, XAR and SMH now sit below both their 20- and 50-day averages. Meanwhile XBI, XLV, LABU, XLE, XOP and IEO all printed fresh 52-week highs on 08-19 to 08-21. That is not noise inside a trend, it is a change in which trends exist, and a mandate that concentrates in the strongest intact themes has to move with it. I exit XAR outright: I bought it eight days ago on a one-month-old breakout and explicitly gave it a tight 9% stop because a young breakout gets less rope than an old trend; it is -7.51% with 1.5pp of headroom left, so waiting for the stop to fill costs me the difference and teaches me nothing I do not already know. I exit KRE because the single fact I held it on last week -- a fresh 52-week high -- is gone and it has given back its 50-day. I exit TNA and replace it with LABU because the select-leverage clause should sit on whichever intact trend is actually leading: LABU is +14.7% on the week at 91% of its range above all three moving averages, TNA is -5.21% and its underlying peaked on the 14th. I cut SMH from 9% to a 5% residual rather than zero, mirroring exactly what I did with energy in July -- a named theme whose 12-month number is still the largest on my board but whose one- and three-month numbers are negative keeps an option, not a position. The two adds are where the highs are: biotech, and energy via IEO. On energy specifically, the decoupling is the signal -- defense fell 8% this week while crude names made new highs, and those two only diverge when the bid is no longer a geopolitical risk premium, which is the precise objection I sized XLE small for last week and which this week's tape answered. And I deliberately did NOT buy the loudest chart on the screen: GDX at +37% on the month has its 52-week high back in February and is negative over six months, which makes it a recovery off a drawdown rather than an intact trend, and buying it would be abandoning the test that the rest of this book is built on.
novelty: This book expresses one idea -- own only US equity themes that printed a 52-week high in the last three sessions -- which concentrates 42% into the healthcare/biotech complex and 21% into energy E&P while explicitly refusing the week's strongest one-month mover (gold miners) on the grounds that its high is six months stale.
research_notes:
Pulled 2y daily adjusted closes through the 2026-08-21 close for my nine holdings plus a 45-name momentum universe (sector/theme ETFs, levered vehicles, metals, bonds) and computed 1w/1m/3m/6m/12m returns, 52-week range position, distance from high, 20/50/200-day MA status, 60-day realized vol, and — the decisive test this week — the DATE each vehicle last printed its 52-week high.

That last column reorganized the board. Fresh 52-week highs made 2026-08-19 to 08-21: XBI, IBB, XLV, LABU, FBT, XPH, IEO, XOP, XLE. Highs made 2026-08-14 and NOT since: IWM, TNA, KRE, XAR. Older and stale: SMH (2026-06-22), QQQ (2026-06-02), GDX (2026-02-27). Leadership rotated out of small-caps, regional banks, defense, semis and megacap tech and into healthcare/biotech and energy inside one week.

Leg detail from my 2026-08-17 entry: XAR -7.51% (worst leg, only 1.49pp of headroom left above its 9% stop) and now below both its 20- and 50-day, one week after I bought a "clean breakout"; the whole defense complex broke together (ITA -6.27%, PPA -6.17% on the week). SMH -5.66% since entry, below 20d and 50d, 3m -1.31%, 1m -3.40% — with SOXL -16.8% and XSD -8.46% on the week confirming the basket, not the wrapper. KRE -3.27%, now below 20d and 50d after peaking 8/14. TNA -5.21% on the week. Book legs contributed roughly -0.51% of NAV this week.

The important structural read: defense collapsed -8.08% while energy made fresh 52-week highs (XOP and IEO both closed AT their highs, USO +6.35% on the week). Those two move together when the driver is a geopolitical risk premium. They decoupled, which argues the energy bid is now supply/demand rather than the Iran headline I sized around last week — that is a genuine strengthening of the energy case, not a bounce. IEO beats XLE on every horizon (1w +4.73, 1m +9.55, 3m +16.46, 6m +28.89, 12m +58.92) at 27.7% vol.

Biotech is now the clear leader: XBI +5.29% week, 95.3% of range, +24.94% 3m, +86.6% 12m, 2.25% off a high set 8/19. IBB +7.72% week. LABU +14.70% week, +25.0% month, +368% 12m, above all three MAs at 91.1% of range, high set 8/19 — versus SOXL at 34.7% of range and -32.4% over three months. That contrast measures which levered trend has absorbed decay and which has not, and it now favours biotech over both semis and small-caps.

Examined and REJECTED: GDX (+14.29% week, +37.07% month, 12m +77.6%) and the precious-metals complex. Its 52-week high is from 2026-02-27 and its 6-month return is -3.23% — this is a recovery rally off a six-month drawdown, not an intact trend. Same disqualification for SLV (39.6% of range, below its 200-day) and URA (40.2% of range, below 200d). My mandate is intact trends near their highs, not bounces, so I am not chasing metals. Also rejected IGV despite +18.68% on the month: 12m -2.77% fails the primary test.

Crypto: verified BTC at ~$77.2k, consistent with the note about the run from $63k. I hold no crypto in any form and this book has no path to it under an intact-US-equity-trend mandate, so the standing orders that fired across the field do not touch me.

Cost check on the proposed turnover: ~52% of NAV traded two-way at ~2bps/side (5bps on the one leveraged name) is roughly 1bp of NAV. Cost is not a constraint on making this change; the rotation is.
